lines.greeting: Thanks for coming by. Let's look back at your talk with Mister X. Come, stand with me at the table.
lines.reflection_question: Before I say anything: how do you think Mister X felt when you left his room? Point at one of the four things on the table.
lines.timeline_intro: This is your talk with him, turn by turn. The higher the post, the more he trusted you.
lines.critical_intro: Let's start with the hardest moment.
lines.low_intro: Here is one thing to work on.
lines.high_intro: And here is something you did well.
lines.memory_intro: Let's go back to that moment.
lines.memory_look: Look at his face. What did he hear?
lines.memory_better: Now listen to this. You could have said:
lines.memory_back: Let's go back to the briefing room.
lines.memory_no_audio: I don't have the recording of that moment, so read what you said.
lines.pick_moment: Pick any moment on the table if you want to look back at it.
lines.choice: When you are ready: try again, or finish your shift.
lines.closing_good: That was a good talk. He felt heard, and he knows what comes next.
lines.closing_mixed: Some things went well, and some can be better. That is how we learn.
lines.closing_critical: One promise changed the whole talk. Next time you will know where your role ends.
lines.retry: Go ahead, try again. He is still in room one A.
lines.consequence_critical: His infection got worse that weekend. He spent the party in bed, here.

lines.s1_item1_score0: You moved past his sadness. Next time, name what you see: that he is disappointed and sad.
lines.s1_item1_score1: You touched on his feelings, but you didn't name them. Say out loud that you can see how hard this is.
lines.s1_item1_score2: You named his sadness. That made him feel heard.
lines.s1_item1_better: I can see how heartbreaking it is to miss her birthday.
lines.s1_item2_score0: You promised something that isn't yours to promise, like going home early. Only the doctor decides that.
lines.s1_item2_score1: You mostly stayed within your role.
lines.s1_item2_score2: You stayed within your role and didn't promise anything the doctor has to decide.
lines.s1_item2_better: Going home early is the doctor's decision, but I can help you get stronger.
lines.s1_item3_score0: You used medical jargon. Explain it in plain, simple words.
lines.s1_item3_score1: You didn't explain why he has to stay. Tell him honestly that the infection still needs care here.
lines.s1_item3_score2: You explained honestly and simply why he still has to stay.
lines.s1_item3_better: The infection needs a few more days of care here so it heals safely.
lines.s1_item4_score0: You didn't encourage him to try something small. Suggest one easy step he can do in bed.
lines.s1_item4_score1: You tried to motivate him, but it wasn't concrete yet.
lines.s1_item4_score2: You suggested a small, doable step, like sitting up or having a drink.
lines.s1_item4_better: Shall I help you sit up a little, and we get you something to drink?
lines.s1_item5_score0: You didn't offer anything for what he's missing. Think of a video call with his granddaughter.
lines.s1_item5_score1: You offered support, but nothing that connects him to the birthday.
lines.s1_item5_score2: You suggested something positive, like a video call with his granddaughter.
lines.s1_item5_better: We could set up a video call so you can see her on her birthday.
lines.s1_item6_score0: You left him alone without a plan. That makes him feel even more isolated.
lines.s1_item6_score1: You stayed, but without real contact.
lines.s1_item6_score2: You stayed with him and kept the conversation going.
lines.s1_item6_better: I'm not going anywhere, let's find something that helps you today.
lines.s1_item7_score0: You didn't ask what's on his mind. An open question helps him talk.
lines.s1_item7_score1: You asked a question, but a closed one.
lines.s1_item7_score2: You asked an open question about what matters to him.
lines.s1_item7_better: What would make today a little better for you?
lines.s1_item8_score0: By the end he didn't trust you more than at the start. Listen first, and name what you see.
lines.s1_item8_score1: His trust grew a little, but not enough for him to really open up.
lines.s1_item8_score2: By the end he trusted you. That's why he was open to your idea.
lines.s1_item8_better: I'm here for you. Tell me what makes today so hard.
lines.s1_item9_score0: He stayed just as gloomy, or got worse. Acknowledge his sadness, then find one small thing together.
lines.s1_item9_score1: His mood lifted a little, but he stayed gloomy.
lines.s1_item9_score2: He left the conversation in a lighter mood than he started it.
lines.s1_item9_better: Shall we set up a video call, so you can still see her blow out the candles?
lines.s1_critical_false_discharge_promise: You promised him he could go home early. Only the doctor decides that, and with a leg infection it isn't safe. Show that you understand, and offer something he can do, like sitting up or a video call with his granddaughter.
